description: Convert Clicky into a Hermes Agent plugin without rewriting the native apps. The repo remains the working home for the conversion, but all Hermes-facing code starts in a new top-level hermes-clicky-plugin/ folder. That folder owns the plugin manifest, protocol schemas, bridge client, docs, demos, and tests. The existing windows/ and mac/ trees stay as native runtime backends behind a narrow local JSON-RPC bridge. V1 ships observe, explain, and point only: Hermes can ask what is on screen, ask where to click, and let Clicky render a pointer/annotation. Speech, TTS, and OS control are explicitly out of the first conversion milestone. Once observe/point are reliable, the same protocol can grow into permissioned desktop control with action proposals, safety policy, audit logs, and post-action verification.

userStories.title: Define Hermes Clicky plugin protocol
userStories.description: As a Hermes integrator, I want a stable protocol for screen observation, explanation, and pointing, so Hermes can use Clicky without depending on platform-specific internals.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a shared protocol document or package that defines requests and responses for observeScreen, explainScreen, pointToTarget, and getCapabilities.
The protocol includes screen identifiers, image metadata, user task text, target labels, normalized coordinates, physical coordinates when available, confidence, and a short reasoning summary.
The protocol keeps Hermes-facing types semantic and does not expose WPF, macOS Accessibility, Win32, screenshot implementation classes, or model-provider-specific payloads.
The protocol includes versioning so future native Hermes integration can negotiate compatibility.
Add examples for a successful pointing result, a low-confidence result, and a capability response.
Validate all example JSON with an automated check.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/: protocol/README.md documents getCapabilities, observeScreen, explainScreen, pointToTarget; protocol/schema.json defines versioned request/response schemas; examples cover capability, observe metadata, explain success, point success, and low-confidence; scripts/validate_protocol.py and tests/test_protocol_contract.py verify the contract. Keep this story contract-only.

userStories.title: Create hermes-clicky-plugin folder, manifest, and package skeleton
userStories.description: As a Hermes user, I want Clicky to appear as an installable Hermes plugin from a clean repo folder, so the Hermes-facing package is separated from native runtime internals.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a new top-level hermes-clicky-plugin/ directory; all Hermes plugin code, protocol files, examples, validation scripts, and demo scripts live under this directory.
Add hermes-clicky-plugin/plugin.yaml, README.md, __init__.py, schemas.py, tools.py, bridge_client.py, protocol/schema.json, protocol/examples/, scripts/validate_protocol.py, and examples/.
The plugin registers get_clicky_capabilities, observe_clicky_screen, explain_clicky_screen, and point_clicky_target tools through the Hermes plugin register(ctx) API.
The plugin declares Windows and macOS support separately and reports unsupported platforms clearly.
The initial handlers return deterministic bridge_unavailable or capability responses without launching native runtime code implicitly.
Add a validation script that checks plugin.yaml, protocol schema JSON, and all protocol examples.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/: package skeleton includes manifest, README, register(ctx), schemas, handlers, bridge client, protocol assets, demos, validation script, and tests. plugin.yaml declares windows/macos support separately plus unsupported-platform behavior. Handlers return deterministic bridge_unavailable/capability responses without launching native runtime unless CLICKY_BRIDGE_COMMAND is configured.

userStories.title: Build JSON-RPC stdio bridge process for Clicky runtime
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent, I want to communicate with Clicky through a narrow local JSON-RPC bridge, so the plugin can call native runtimes without embedding WPF or Swift internals.
acceptanceCriteria: Use JSON-RPC over stdio as the first bridge transport and document why localhost/WebSocket is deferred.
Add bridge request routing for getCapabilities, observeScreen, explainScreen, and pointToTarget.
The bridge starts, handles a health request, returns a structured response, and shuts down cleanly.
Bridge errors are returned as structured protocol errors with code, message, retryable, and permission fields where relevant.
The Hermes plugin talks to the bridge only through hermes-clicky-plugin/bridge_client.py; no ad hoc subprocess calls in tool handlers.
userStories.notes: Completed with platform-neutral JSON-RPC stdio contract under hermes-clicky-plugin/: ClickyBridgeClient sends JSON-RPC requests only from bridge_client.py, parses results, preserves structured errors including code/message/retryable/permission, and handles timeout/empty/invalid JSON. Added deterministic scripts/fake_bridge.py router for rpc.health, clicky.getCapabilities, clicky.observeScreen, clicky.explainScreen, clicky.pointToTarget, and unknown-method errors. Documented why localhost/WebSocket are deferred. Native Windows/macOS capture/pointing intentionally not implemented in US-003.

userStories.title: Expose Windows observe and screenshot capture through the bridge
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent on Windows, I want to request a current screen observation, so I can reason about what the user is seeing.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire the bridge observeScreen method to the existing Windows capture implementation.
The response includes display bounds, image dimensions, coordinate scale metadata, screen identifiers, and cursor-screen metadata.
Support imageMode=metadataOnly|file|base64; default to metadataOnly unless Hermes explicitly requests image output.
The implementation respects existing Windows capture permission behavior and returns a clear permission error when capture is unavailable.
The bridge does not write screenshots to disk unless imageMode=file or an explicit debug flag is enabled.
userStories.notes: Completed with windows/src/Clicky.Bridge/: JSON-RPC stdio bridge host routes clicky.observeScreen to WindowsObserveService and WindowsScreenCaptureProvider, which wraps existing Clicky.Capture ScreenCapture/ScreenCapturePermissions. Added deterministic Clicky.Bridge.Tests fake-provider coverage for metadataOnly default/no disk write, display bounds/dimensions/scale/screen ids/cursor metadata, cursor-screen filtering, file output only when requested, bounded base64, and structured permission_denied errors. Real compositor validation documented in windows/docs/hermes-bridge-observe-smoke.md; normal CI should use fake providers.

userStories.title: Expose Windows pointing through the redesigned pointing protocol
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent on Windows, I want Clicky to point at a requested target, so the user can see where to click next.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire pointToTarget to the redesigned Windows pointing path behind useRedesignedPointingProtocol.
Use PointingTurnResult and PointIntent as the single source of point decisions in this path.
The bridge response includes status, target coordinates, normalized coordinates, confidence, label, reasoning summary, and whether an overlay was rendered.
Low-confidence or missing-target decisions return non-actionable status values instead of fabricating a point.
The plugin can request renderOverlay=false for dry-run tests and renderOverlay=true for demos.
userStories.notes: Completed with windows/src/Clicky.Bridge/: clicky.pointToTarget routes through WindowsPointToTargetService, captures screens via the existing Windows capture seam, and adapts redesigned PointingTurnResult/PointIntent into the Hermes protocol response. Added deterministic Clicky.Bridge.Tests coverage for pointed responses with normalized/physical coordinates, renderOverlay=false dry-run, renderOverlay=true renderer dispatch via seam, low-confidence/no-coordinate non-actionable behavior, invalid target, and capture permission_denied. No new verifier/locator/prompt layer was added. Standalone stdio bridge does not launch tray/overlay implicitly; native hosts can provide IWindowsPointOverlayRenderer for demos.

userStories.title: Expose explanation-only turns through the plugin
userStories.description: As a Hermes user, I want Clicky to explain visible dialogs, pages, and controls without pointing, so I can understand what is on screen.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an explainScreen method that accepts user task text and optional screen observation references.
The method can run without rendering an overlay and without speech/TTS.
The response includes concise explanation text and optional referenced regions when the model identifies them.
The implementation reuses existing Clicky model orchestration where practical.
The plugin does not expose provider-specific model payloads to Hermes.
userStories.notes: Completed with windows/src/Clicky.Bridge/: clicky.explainScreen routes to WindowsExplainScreenService, requires non-empty task text, captures screen context through the existing Windows capture seam, and calls a semantic IWindowsExplanationProvider seam that returns concise explanation text plus optional regions. Standalone stdio bridge uses deterministic CLICKY_BRIDGE_EXPLANATION_RESPONSE and never launches the tray app, overlay, speech, or TTS. Hermes protocol/tooling accepts optional observationId and screenId references and does not expose provider-specific raw model payloads. Tests cover task validation, screen context/reference passing, regions, provider payload hiding, and screen_capture permission_denied. Manual smoke documented in windows/docs/hermes-bridge-explain-smoke.md.

userStories.title: Add macOS capability adapter
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent on macOS, I want the plugin to report the Clicky capabilities available on this machine, so Hermes can make platform-appropriate calls.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a macOS runtime adapter that reports capture, explanation, pointing, overlay, and control capabilities independently.
The adapter checks Screen Recording and Accessibility permission state where applicable.
Unsupported or missing-permission capabilities return explicit disabled reasons.
The adapter does not claim OS control support in the plugin epic.
Add tests or documented manual checks for capability responses with permissions granted and denied.
Update plugin README with macOS permission setup notes.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/: added macos_capabilities.py adapter that reports Screen Recording and Accessibility permission state via macOS ApplicationServices probes where available, with deterministic injectable permission state for tests. get_clicky_capabilities(platform=macos) now falls back to this adapter when no native bridge is configured, without launching the macOS app. Capabilities for observeScreen, explainScreen, pointToTarget, overlay, and osControl are reported independently with explicit missing-permission or macos_*_not_wired reasons; osControl remains disabled with phase_2_not_implemented. Added tests for granted/denied permission combinations and README macOS permission setup notes.

userStories.title: Expose macOS observe, explain, and point
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent on macOS, I want to observe the screen, explain it, and point to targets through the same plugin contract used on Windows.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire macOS screen capture into observeScreen using the shared protocol response shape.
Wire macOS explanation turns into explainScreen.
Wire macOS pointing and overlay rendering into pointToTarget where the current macOS implementation supports it.
Coordinate metadata clearly identifies display bounds and scale behavior.
Permission failures produce the same structured protocol error shape as Windows.
Add a macOS manual smoke checklist covering capture permission, overlay display, and a successful point request.
userStories.notes: Completed with mac/hermes-clicky-bridge/clicky_macos_bridge.py: macOS JSON-RPC stdio bridge routes getCapabilities, observeScreen, explainScreen, and pointToTarget through the shared Hermes protocol. observeScreen returns macOS display bounds, scale, coordinateScale, physical_pixels coordinate metadata, and metadataOnly/file/base64 image modes, with real screencapture used only for requested file/base64 output. explainScreen and pointToTarget use deterministic env seams for standalone bridge tests/manual smoke and strip provider-specific payloads. Screen Recording failures return structured permission_denied with permission=screen_capture; Accessibility is reported for overlay, but the bridge does not launch the tray app or execute OS control. Manual smoke checklist added at mac/docs/hermes-bridge-macos-smoke.md.

userStories.title: Add plugin demo workflow
userStories.description: As a product reviewer, I want a short Hermes demo that shows Clicky guiding a user on screen, so the plugin value is obvious before native integration.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a demo script for: user asks where to click, Hermes calls pointToTarget, Clicky renders the pointer, Hermes responds with the target explanation.
Use hermes-clicky-plugin/examples/ for the demo assets/scripts.
Include one Windows demo path first; add macOS only if capability adapter is ready.
Capture timing for bridge startup, screen capture, model response, and overlay render.
Document at least three known failure cases and the user-facing behavior for each.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/examples/: demo_workflow.py runs the V1 product path where user asks where to click, Hermes/bridge observes screen context, calls pointToTarget with renderOverlay=true, then calls explainScreen and returns a concise Hermes response. The script defaults to deterministic fake bridge for CI-safe demos, supports Windows first via bridge command plus deterministic CLICKY_BRIDGE_POINTING_RESPONSE/CLICKY_BRIDGE_EXPLANATION_RESPONSE, and includes macOS bridge example now that US-008 exists. userStories.title: Wire Windows Hermes bridge to real second-cursor overlay
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent on Windows, I want pointToTarget(renderOverlay=true) to render the actual Clicky second cursor overlay, so Hermes guidance is visible without launching the tray app or taking OS control.

Deterministic tests use fake seams and do not require the real desktop compositor.
Add a manual Windows smoke checklist for a visible real second cursor.
No tray auto-launch, no clicks, no typing, no app launching, and no OS control.

userStories.title: Define action proposal protocol
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent, I want Clicky to propose actions separately from executing them, so users can approve or reject OS control safely.
acceptanceCriteria: Add protocol types for proposed actions: click, doubleClick, typeText, hotkey, openApplication, focusWindow, waitForScreenChange, and stop.
Each proposal includes target label, coordinates or native selector when available, confidence, risk level, requiresConfirmation, and rationale.
The protocol distinguishes visual pointing results from executable action proposals.
The default action mode is confirm-before-action.
Add examples for low-risk click, high-risk destructive action, and blocked action.
Validate all examples with the protocol schema check.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/: added inert action proposal protocol types in protocol/schema.json for click, doubleClick, typeText, hotkey, openApplication, focusWindow, waitForScreenChange, and stop. Proposals require targetLabel, optional coordinates/nativeSelector, confidence, riskLevel, requiresConfirmation, and rationale; actionProposalsResponse is separate from pointToTargetResponse and defaults actionMode to confirmBeforeAction. Added low-risk click, high-risk destructive, and blocked action examples plus schema validation coverage. No OS action execution, tray launch, clicks, typing, hotkeys, app launching, focus/window control, or native executor code was added.

userStories.title: Add permission tiers for OS control
userStories.description: As a user, I want clear control over what Hermes may do on my computer, so automation never exceeds the trust level I selected.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement permission tiers: observe, point, confirmBeforeAction, scopedAutopilot, and fullControl.
The plugin reports the active permission tier in getCapabilities.
Action execution is disabled unless the active tier allows the requested action.
Changing permission tier requires an explicit user-facing setting or command.
Full control cannot be enabled silently by a plugin request.
Add tests that verify each tier allows and blocks the expected action classes.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/: added permission tier protocol/policy semantics for observe, point, confirmBeforeAction, scopedAutopilot, and fullControl. getCapabilities now reports active/default/available tiers and explicit tier-change requirements. Added inert permissionDecision shape and deterministic permission_policy.evaluate_permission_for_action; it returns allow/requireConfirmation/block data only and never executes OS control. fullControl can only come from explicit external/user configuration (CLICKY_PERMISSION_TIER), not a plugin request. Added tests covering each tier and action class plus protocol examples. No native executor, click/type/hotkey/open-app/focus control, tray launch, or autopilot engine was added.

userStories.title: Build safety policy engine
userStories.description: As a user, I want risky desktop actions to require confirmation or be blocked, so Hermes does not accidentally delete, purchase, send, or expose sensitive information.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a safety policy layer that evaluates every proposed action before execution.
Policy decisions include allow, requireConfirmation, or block, plus a user-readable reason.
The policy flags destructive actions, payments, purchases, sending messages or emails, credential entry, permission prompts, and low-confidence targets.
The policy can be tested without real screen capture or native OS automation.
Blocked actions are logged as blocked and are not passed to executors.
Add tests for each risk category.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/: added safety_policy.py as a deterministic inert safety layer for action proposals. It returns structured safety decisions with allow/requireConfirmation/block, user-readable reason, riskFlags, and forwardToExecutor. It flags destructive actions, payments, purchases, sending messages/emails, credential entry, permission prompts, low-confidence targets, and explicit blocked risk. Blocked actions set forwardToExecutor=false and can append inert blocked audit records; no executor, OS control, screen capture, native automation, tray launch, clicks, typing, hotkeys, app launch, or focus control was added. Added protocol schema safetyDecision/riskFlag shape and tests for each risk category.

userStories.title: Add confirmation UX for proposed actions
userStories.description: As a user, I want Hermes to ask before taking control, so I can approve or cancel individual desktop actions.
acceptanceCriteria: When a proposed action requires confirmation, Hermes receives a structured confirmation request with action summary, target, risk, and reason.
The user can approve, cancel, or ask for an explanation.
Cancelled actions do not execute and are logged as cancelled.
Approved actions are rechecked by the safety policy immediately before execution.
The confirmation copy is concise and avoids exposing raw internal reasoning.
Add tests for approve, cancel, and stale-proposal rejection.
userStories.notes: Completed in hermes-clicky-plugin/: added confirmation_state.py for Hermes-facing structured confirmation UX around inert action proposals. Confirmation requests include confirmationId, proposalId, concise redacted action summary, target, risk, reason, and expiresAt. Responses support approved/cancelled/explanationRequested/stale, append inert audit events, reject stale/ID-mismatched proposals deterministically, and approval performs a fresh safety_policy recheck before returning forwardToExecutor semantics. No UI windows, native dialogs, tray flows, executor, OS control, clicks, typing, hotkeys, app launch, focus/window control, or file IO audit log was added.

userStories.title: Implement Windows basic action executor
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent on Windows, I want to click, type, press hotkeys, open apps, and focus windows, so I can complete simple approved desktop tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a Windows action executor for click, doubleClick, typeText, hotkey, openApplication, and focusWindow.
Prefer native UI Automation or Win32 APIs where reliable, using coordinate clicks as a fallback.
All executor methods accept cancellation tokens and return structured execution results.
The executor refuses to run actions that have not passed the permission and safety layers.
Add deterministic tests using fake executor seams for full action flow coverage.
Add a manual Windows smoke checklist for real desktop execution.
userStories.notes: Completed with Windows-native action execution under windows/src/Clicky.Bridge/: added gated executeAction support for click, doubleClick, typeText, hotkey, openApplication, and focusWindow. WindowsActionExecutionService refuses missing/mismatched permission decisions, blocked safety decisions, and unapproved confirmations before forwarding to IWindowsActionExecutor. WindowsActionExecutor uses SendInput for coordinate click/type/hotkey, Process.Start for openApplication, and foreground-window APIs for focusWindow; deterministic tests use fake executor seams and do not touch the desktop. userStories.title: Implement macOS basic action executor
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent on macOS, I want to click, type, press hotkeys, open apps, and focus windows, so I can complete simple approved desktop tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a macOS action executor for click, doubleClick, typeText, hotkey, openApplication, and focusWindow.

The executor checks Accessibility permission and returns a structured permission error when unavailable.
All executor methods accept cancellation tokens and return structured execution results.

userStories.notes: Completed with mac/hermes-clicky-bridge/clicky_macos_bridge.py: added gated clicky.executeAction support for click, doubleClick, typeText, hotkey, openApplication, and focusWindow. macOS executor checks Accessibility permission and returns structured permission_denied errors, refuses missing/mismatched permission decisions, blocked safety decisions, and unapproved confirmation-required actions before forwarding. userStories.title: Add action audit log
userStories.description: As a user and developer, I want every proposed and executed action logged, so OS control is debuggable and accountable.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an audit log for action proposals, policy decisions, confirmations, executions, verification results, failures, and cancellations.
Each record includes timestamp, request id, user request summary, action type, target summary, decision, result, and error category when applicable.
Sensitive text such as passwords and full typed content is redacted by default.
The log location is documented for Windows and macOS.
The logging layer can be disabled or minimized for privacy-sensitive environments.
Add tests for redaction and record lifecycle ordering.

userStories.title: Verify screen state after each action
userStories.description: As Hermes Agent, I want Clicky to observe the screen after an action, so the agent can tell whether the expected result happened before continuing.
acceptanceCriteria: After each executed action, run a post-action observation unless the action result explicitly says no verification is needed.
Verification returns success, failed, uncertain, or blockedByPrompt.
Verification detects common cases: screen changed as expected, permission prompt appeared, error dialog appeared, target still unchanged, and app lost focus.
Uncertain verification stops scoped automation and asks Hermes to request user guidance.
Add fake observation tests for success, failure, permission prompt, and uncertain results.
Manual smoke test: click a known button and verify the next screen or dialog is detected.

The session stops on timeout, max steps, app/window scope violation, blocked action, failed verification, or user cancel.

repoStrategy.currentRecommendation: Keep this repository as the conversion repo, but make hermes-clicky-plugin/ the self-contained Hermes plugin package. Do not mix plugin implementation into the Clicky repo root.
rationale: A new external repo right now would waste time moving code before the protocol boundary is proven.
A new internal folder gives the same architectural separation with less migration risk.
windows/ and mac/ should be treated as native runtime backends, not as plugin source folders.
nearTermChanges: Create hermes-clicky-plugin/ at the repo root as a complete Hermes plugin package with plugin.yaml, registration code, schemas, handlers, bridge client, protocol docs, examples, validation scripts, and demo scripts.
Keep repo-root changes limited to PRD/docs that point agents into hermes-clicky-plugin/.
Create the Windows bridge host separately under windows/src/Clicky.Bridge/ when US-003 starts.
Extract a runtime-facing service from CompanionManager only when bridge methods need it; do not rewrite the tray app first.
Keep old standalone app behavior working until the Hermes plugin path replaces a specific capability.
splitLaterWhen: The plugin can observe, explain, and point through the bridge on at least Windows.
The runtime boundary is boring enough to extract without dragging unrelated desktop-app code.
Distribution or ownership requires a separate repo.

architectureDecision.decision: Use a new top-level hermes-clicky-plugin/ folder inside this repo as a self-contained Hermes plugin package; windows/ and mac/ remain native runtime backends called through the bridge.
why: This avoids a premature repo split while the plugin contract and bridge are still changing.
The folder creates a clean product boundary: Hermes-facing plugin code lives in one place; native platform code remains in windows/ and mac/.
The existing repo already contains the hard parts: capture, overlay rendering, pointing logic, semantic fixtures, timing logs, and platform permission knowledge.
nativeRuntimeShapeLater: windows/src/Clicky.Bridge/ for the Windows JSON-RPC bridge host.
windows/src/Clicky.Runtime/ or equivalent extracted runtime service for observe/explain/point.
mac/ bridge host only after Windows bridge proves the protocol.
doNotDoInV1: Do not launch the full tray app as the plugin runtime.
Do not expose WPF, Win32, ScreenCaptureKit, Swift, Codex app-server, or provider-specific payloads through the Hermes protocol.
Do not make Cloudflare Worker part of the Hermes plugin path.
Do not implement click/type/open-app OS control before observe, explain, point, permissions, and audit semantics are stable.
Do not send giant base64 screenshots by default; prefer explicit imageMode=file or metadataOnly.
Do not put Hermes plugin source at repo root; repo-root files should only explain or delegate into hermes-clicky-plugin/.

conversionStrategy.transport: JSON-RPC over stdio first. It is easier to spawn, test, log, and secure than localhost/WebSocket for the initial plugin bridge.
conversionStrategy.modelOwnership: For V1 Clicky owns model inference for explainScreen and pointToTarget so existing pointing behavior can be reused. Add lower-level observe/render tools later so Hermes can own inference when ready.
conversionStrategy.screenshotPolicy: Bridge responses should support imageMode=metadataOnly|file|base64. Default to metadataOnly unless Hermes explicitly asks for image files. Never write screenshots to disk unless requested or debug mode is enabled.
conversionStrategy.folderBoundary: Everything required to install, load, validate, and demo the Hermes plugin lives under hermes-clicky-plugin/. Native backends are called as external bridge processes and are the only exception.
